title: PointND.Float.getCoord throws past its stored length: a point whose trailing coordinates are 0 (e.g. y = 0) crashes getY
description: PointND.Float(float...) and PointND.Double(double...) both trim trailing zero coordinates when they store a point, so (5, 0) is stored as [5]. Double.getCoord(dim) returns 0.0 for a dim past the stored array (PointND.java ~840); Float.getCoord(dim) indexes the array directly (PointND.java ~539), so getY() on a Float point with y = 0 throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException. Found by TRADE-21 with a trade City at y = 0. Give Float.getCoord the same past-the-end rule as Double, and check every other Float accessor that indexes fs directly.
definition-of-done:
1. PointND.Float.getCoord and every Float accessor return 0 for a dimension past the stored coordinates, as Double does.
2. A unit test builds Float and Double points with trailing zeros and reads every dimension.
3. A trade City at y = 0 works.
testing-plan:
1. Unit test for Float/Double points (5,0), (0,0), (1,0,0).
2. Full suite.
